chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sind ibn Muhammad from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who killed his mother, saying: 'If it was accidental, then he inherits her, and if he killed her intentionally, then he does not inherit her.'
ai.seo_question: Does a killer inherit from the victim in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records a legal ruling (qada) by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the inheritance of a father who kills his mother, distinguishing between accidental and intentional homicide. It establishes that an accidental killer still inherits, while an intentional killer is barred from inheriting. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that *qatl al-khat'i* (accidental killing) does not trigger the *ghulul* (plundering) principle that excludes the killer from inheritance, unlike *qatl al-mutammim* (intentional killing).
